name: file
summary: Works out the real type of a file.
description: On Linux, a file extension is only a convention. file examines the contents (the first bytes, called the “magic number”) to tell what a file really is: text and its encoding, image, archive, executable, script…

options.description: Does not print the file name before the result.
Prints the MIME type (image/png, text/plain; charset=utf-8…).
Follows symbolic links and describes the target.

examples.output:
photo.jpg: JPEG image data, JFIF standard 1.01, 1920x1080
script.sh: Bourne-Again shell script, ASCII text executable

examples.explanation: Checks that a file really is what its extension claims.
examples.output: document.pdf: Zip archive data, at least v2.0 to extract

examples.explanation: MIME type and encoding of a text file.

examples.output: /bin/ls: ELF 64-bit LSB pie executable, x86-64, dynamically linked
